title: Yassa au Poulet
localName: Yassa au poulet — ma recette inratable
author: Aïssatou Mbaye
desc: Her no-fail yassa — the seasoning pounded and split two-thirds to one-third, the chicken stuffed with roff, grilled at 220 degrees for forty minutes.
longDesc: A Senegalese cook's own version, and the structure is the lesson: the pounded seasoning is divided, a third reserved for the sauce and two-thirds mixed with lemon juice, salt, pepper and oil for the chicken. The chicken is cut into medium pieces, incisions made and stuffed with roff, coated with the marinade and refrigerated at least two hours. Then a tablespoon of mustard is brushed on and it grills at 220 degrees for forty minutes, turned halfway. The sauce is onions softened until translucent with the reserved third, cooked until you get a good caramel colour. Her mother's line: making a yassa is easy, but making a good yassa is not so simple.
ingredients: 1 tbsp mustard — appears in the method, not the printed list
steps: Pound the garlic, spring onions, bell pepper, chillies and coriander into a seasoning paste.
Reserve 1/3 of the pounded seasoning for the sauce.
Add the lemon juice, salt, pepper and olive oil to the other 2/3.
Cut the chicken into medium pieces, make incisions and stuff them with the roff.
Coat the chicken with the 2/3 marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Brush the chicken with 1 tablespoon of mustard.
Grill at 220 degrees for 40 minutes, turning halfway.
Heat oil and add the onions with a bay leaf, stirring often.
Once the onions turn translucent, add the reserved third of the seasoning, salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat until you get a good caramel colour.
Serve the chicken with the sauce.
chefTips: Split the seasoning before the lemon goes in. A third stays dry for the sauce; two-thirds get the acid and the oil for the chicken. Mixing it all together loses you the sauce's backbone.
Until you get a good caramel colour — her sauce endpoint, and it is a colour not a clock.
Stuff the incisions with roff as well as coating the outside. Two layers of seasoning, which is the Senegalese approach to any protein.
Two hours minimum in the fridge. She does not offer a shortcut and there is not one.
Two hundred and twenty degrees for forty minutes, turned halfway. That is hot and fast, which is what gives colour without drying the pieces.
Her mother's line is worth keeping in mind: making a yassa is easy, but making a good yassa is not so simple. The difference is in the onions.

Note an internal contradiction in the source — the introduction says there is no mustard in the sauce while step six brushes the chicken with a tablespoon of it. Both appear on the page and neither is corrected here.
commonMistakes: Mixing all the seasoning with the lemon, leaving nothing for the sauce.
Only coating the chicken rather than stuffing the incisions.
Pulling the sauce before it reaches caramel colour.
sources: Adapted from 'Yassa au Poulet : ma recette inratable', aistoucuisine.com, path /publications/yassa-au-poulet. BYLINE: Aïssatou Mbaye. Date as printed: 25 septembre 2015. Yield: NONE PRINTED. Line-level agreement: TWO-PASS on every figure. No Wolof name is printed.

Marinade ingredients as printed in French: '2 citrons'; '6 gousses d'ail'; '2 oignons cebette (oignons vert) ou 1 oignon'; '1 poivron rouge'; '2 piments végétariens (facultatif)'; '1 bonne poignée de coriandre (facultatif)'; '2 cuillères à soupe d'huile d'olive'; 'Sel poivre' with NO quantity; and '1 cuillère à soupe de moutarde', which APPEARS IN STEP 6 AND NOT IN THE INGREDIENT LIST.
TWO ABSENCES, both confirmed across two passes: NO QUANTITY IS PRINTED for the chicken itself, and none for the sauce onions. The five servings above is editorial.

Method figures, TWO-PASS: reserve 1/3 of the pounded seasoning for the sauce and add the lemon juice, salt, pepper and oil to the other 2/3; cut the chicken into medium pieces, make incisions and stuff them with le roff — NAMED IN STEP 4 BUT NEVER LISTED AS AN INGREDIENT; coat with the 2/3 marinade and refrigerate 'pendant au moins 2 heures'; brush with '1 cuillère à soupe de moutarde', then 'faire griller à 220°C pendant 40 minutes', turning halfway.

DONENESS CUES as printed in French: 'lorsqu'ils deviennent translucides' for the onions; 'jusqu'à obtenir une belle couleur caramel' for the sauce; and her own 'Aucun moyen de le rater' — no way to get it wrong.

AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, flagged as printed and not reconciled: the introduction states 'pas de moutarde dans la sauce' — no mustard in the sauce — while step six instructs brushing the chicken with a tablespoon of mustard. Both passes saw this.

CULTURAL REMARKS as printed: « Faire un Yassa, c'est facile… mais faire un bon Yassa, ce n'est pas si simple ! » disait ma mère — making a yassa is easy but making a good one is not so simple, said her mother. She states the dish ORIGINATES IN CASAMANCE, which is the attribution this collection follows in the community field, and that the chicken was traditionally grilled over a wood fire.

TWO FURTHER YASSA MARINADES BY THE SAME AUTHOR, recorded here rather than published as their own entries BECAUSE NEITHER PAGE PRINTS ANY METHOD AT ALL — confirmed absent on both passes in both cases, so neither can be published as a recipe without inventing its method. (1) 'Yassa poulet au four', 27 mars 2025: '1 poivron rouge · 3 oignons verts · 2 piments végétariens · 6 gousses d'ails · coriandre (no quantity) · 2 citrons · 1 c. à soupe de moutarde · 3 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive · sel (no quantity) · poivre (no quantity)'. DESPITE ITS TITLE — au four, in the oven — NO OVEN TEMPERATURE AND NO BAKING TIME APPEAR. Note it diverges from the 2015 recipe above at 3 tbsp olive oil and 3 spring onions against 2 tbsp and 2; both are two-pass on their own pages and are NOT harmonised. On that page she calls yassa 'le tout premier plat que j'ai appris à cuisiner' — the very first dish she learned to cook — presents nokoss as the house seasoning pounded at the start, and notes that normally there is no mustard in yassa but that this oven version adds it to get a caramelised colour. (2) 'Yassa aux brochettes de bœuf', 8 novembre 2025: marinade of '2 citrons · 6 gousses d'ails · 2 oignons verts · 1 poivron rouge · 2 piments végétariens · 1 poignée de coriandre · 2 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive · sel · poivre', and for the skewers '600 g de viande bœuf (rumsteck, filet, bavette) · 1 poivron vert · 1 poivron rouge · brochettes en bois'. A QUANTITY-ONLY ENTRY: no times, no temperatures, no cues. Her remark there: 'le Yassa se prête à mille variations' — yassa lends itself to a thousand variations. Note the spelling '6 gousses d'ails' with a plural, which recurs across her newer posts.

A RETRIEVAL NOTE: this site is JavaScript-rendered and its ingredient lists were only partially reachable by the retrieval layer. The figures here came from a structured data-extraction pass rather than verbatim transcription, because verbatim quotation beyond roughly 125 characters is refused.
reheating: Oven for the chicken; warm the sauce separately.
healthBenefits: Two lemons' juice is a real source of vitamin C.
Coriander and bell pepper add vitamin A and antioxidants.
Grilled rather than fried, with only two tablespoons of added oil.
culturalNote: Calling a recipe inratable — no-fail — and then quoting your mother saying a good yassa is not so simple is a very Senegalese kind of confidence. The Casamance attribution she gives matters: yassa is a southern dish that conquered the country, and the wood fire it was grilled over is what the 220-degree oven is standing in for.
